chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nuḍr ibn Suwayd from Zur'ah from Abū Baṣīr said:
I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: The slaughtered animal of the Nāṣib is not permissible.

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: The Nāṣib (one who is hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of the Nāṣib halal to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* establishes the imperibility of meat slaughtered by the *Nāṣib*, a term in Shia jurisprudence denoting those who harbor enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly the Imams. It extends the concept of ritual purity (*ṭahārah*) beyond mere physical cleanliness to include theological stance, rendering their slaughter invalid for Shia consumption due to their spiritual impurity (*najāsah*). This ruling underscores the link between doctrinal loyalty and legal permissibility in Shia fiqh.
